news.title: How Flamingos World Cup performance makes women football outstanding in Nigeria
news.lede: November 5, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. Nigeria’s qualification for the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup has added another remarkable chapter to the country’s history of breaking new ground in women’s football, reinforcing its position as the first African nation to achieve several significant milestones on the global stage. The Flamingos became the first African team to reach the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Brazil 3-1 in Wednesday’s semi-final in Morocco, blueprint reports. But beyond the immediate excitement of reaching their maiden final, the achievement represents another milestone in a legacy built over decades by different generations of Nigerian female footballers.

news.title: Mexico 2026: Black Challenge face Angola in World Cup opener
news.lede: GHANA’S Black Challenge will begin their quest for international glory at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup with a tough Group D opener against former world champions Angola on Saturday, November 14, in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. The reigning African champions will take on the 2018 World Cup winners at San Martin before facing Colombia the following day at Santa Lucia 1. Ghana will conclude their group-stage campaign against Iraq on Monday, November 16, at Santa Lucia 2. The tournament, scheduled for November 13–22, 2026, will feature 24 national teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, with Ghana aiming to translate their impressive continental achievements into success on the global stage.

news.title: U17 Women's World Cup: Nigeria stun Brazil to set up final date with Japan
news.lede: A goal from Queen Joseph and a brace from Awawu Bashiru secured the historic victory for Akeem Busari's side at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat. The Flamingos went into the encounter full of confidence after beating Venezuela 1-0 in the quarter-finals, thanks to an 89th-minute penalty from captain Azeezat Oduntan. On the other side, the South Americans had defeated China 2-1 in the quarter-finals after overcoming Poland 8-7 on penalties in the round of 16. Nigeria started brightly against Brazil and created several scoring opportunities in the first half with Joseph, Mary Dunstan and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi all going close to breaking the deadlock, but goalkeeper Nathy and her defence kept Nigeria at bay.

news.title: ALL ABOUT REFORMS: Flamingos' Coach Says Reaching FIFA Women's U-17 World Cup Final Is 'Plus For Nigerian Football'
news.lede: A hint emerged on Wednesday at the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco about ongoing reforms for Nigerian football, which were set in motion in August by the National Sports Commission (NSC), Sports247 reports. While nothing concrete has been said about a formalisation committee that will midwife the expected reforms into reality, the country’s female cadet national team, Flamingos’ coach, Akeem Busari believes his team’s strides will set the ball rolling. Read Also: ‘Flamingos African Strength And Their Counter Attacks Overwhelmed My Team,’ Brazil’s Coach Confesses. Busari insinuated as much while speaking in the wake of his team’s 3-1 victory over Brazil in the second semi-final of the ongoing Female Cadet Mundial in Morocco, thereby securing a spot in Saturday’s final, which he tagged ‘a plus for Nigerian football.’

news.title: Borthwick given RFU backing for World Cup even if England flop in Nations Championship
news.lede: RFU chief Bill Sweeney offers full support to Borthwick. England boosted by fly-half Fin Smith’s return to training. Steve Borthwick has been given the Rugby Football Union’s unequivocal backing to lead England into the World Cup next year even if the team flop this autumn. Borthwick’s contract was extended in September to end after the 2028 Six Nations – despite England posting their worst Six Nations performance this year – to avoid speculation in the buildup to the tournament next year.

news.title: Nigeria reach FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup final after defeating Brazil
news.lede: Nigeria have qualified for the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after beating Brazil 3-1 in Wednesday’s semi-final. The Flamingos will face Japan in the final as they seek to claim the world title, following a convincing performance against the South Americans. The Nigerians secured their place in the decisive match with an impressive second-half display. After a goalless first half, the Flamingos broke the deadlock in the 55th minute through Queen Joseph.
